claims.text: The alloy under study is Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
As-cast Al0.1CrCoFeNi has dominant chemical clustering and a largely disordered atomic arrangement.
Heat treatment at 500–700 °C for 5–15 minutes under inert atmosphere induces a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
The heat-treated samples will have greater short-range atomic order than the as-cast baseline.
Increasing short-range chemical order increases the local electronic density of states.
Increasing short-range chemical order modifies phonon dispersion or the vibrational spectrum.
Ordering-induced electronic and phonon changes alter electron–phonon coupling strength.
Electron–phonon coupling mediates conventional BCS-type superconductivity in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Enhanced short-range ordering may elevate the superconducting transition temperature Tc.
Enhanced short-range ordering changes the superconducting gap magnitude.
Pair-correlation functions can be used to identify ordering and clustering in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Warren–Cowley short-range-order parameters describe pair correlations and distinguish clustering from finite-wave-vector ordering.
TEM and XRD pair-distribution analysis can quantify the proposed degree of nanoscale ordering versus clustering.
The ordering mechanism is applicable to HEAs with conventional phonon-mediated superconductivity but may not apply to unconventional superconductors.
The controlled comparison changes only the induced ordering state.
A lack of a consistent statistically significant Tc and gap shift, or a lack of correlation with short-range order, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The comparison is described as differing only in induced ordering, but the treated specimens are described as cold-rolled while the baseline is as-cast. Cold rolling and subsequent heat treatment introduce processing differences beyond ordering, so the stated single-variable control is internally inconsistent.
